heroHeadline: Russia Kills 27 in Single Day, Violates Ukraine's Ceasefire Within Minutes — Ukraine Strikes 1,200 km Into Russia With New 'Flamingo' Missile
heroSubtitle: Russian guided aerial bombs killed 27 Ukrainians on May 5 — 12 in Zaporizhzhia, 6 in Kramatorsk, 4 in Dnipro — the deadliest single day of 2026, as Russia also hit Naftogaz gas facilities killing 5 (including 2 rescuers deliberately struck in a 'double tap'). Ukraine responded by deploying its new FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missile for the first time, reaching a Shahed/Iskander electronics plant 1,200 km inside Russia in Cheboksary, while also knocking out the Kirishi oil refinery in Leningrad Oblast. Ukraine's self-declared open-ended ceasefire took effect at midnight May 6 — Russia violated it within minutes with 3 missiles and 108 drones, racking up 1,820 documented violations by 10 AM.
footerNote: Data sourced from official government reports, UN monitoring missions, major international outlets, and institutional analyses. Historical data draws on peer-reviewed scholarship. Casualty figures are contested; ranges reflect scholarly and official estimates.
